name: Government
topics: Basic concepts: power, authority, legitimacy, sovereignty, democracy
Forms of government: unitary, federal, confederal, monarchy, republic
Organs of government and separation of powers, checks and balances
Rule of law and fundamental human rights
Political parties, party systems and pressure groups
Elections, electoral systems and electoral bodies
Citizenship, public opinion and political socialisation
Pre-colonial political systems: Hausa-Fulani, Yoruba, Igbo
Colonial administration: indirect rule, British and French policies
Nationalism in Nigeria and West Africa
Post-independence constitutions and federalism in Nigeria
International organisations: UN, AU, ECOWAS, Commonwealth, OPEC

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the concept of power in political science?
o: The moral right of a government to make and enforce laws
The supreme legal authority of a state to govern its territory
The general acceptance of a ruler by the citizens
The ability of an individual or group to make others act in accordance with their wishes
questions.e: Power is essentially the capacity or ability to influence the behavior of others, often through the use of coercion or persuasion. It is distinct from authority, which requires moral right and institutional backing.
questions.p: Power na di ability wey person get to make other people do wetoung wey im want, even if dem no gree. E different from authority, wey come with legal backing.

questions.q: In a democratic state, political authority is primarily derived from which of the following?
o: Inherited royal lineage and traditional customs
The mandate given by the electorate through periodic elections
Military might and control of the security apparatus
Economic dominance by multinational corporations
questions.e: In a democracy, authority is legitimate because it is conferred by the people through free and fair elections. This gives the government the moral and legal right to exercise power.
questions.p: For democracy, authority dey come from di people through free and fair election. Dat mandate na im give government di right to rule.

questions.q: What distinguishes authority from power?
o: Authority carries moral and institutional legitimacy, whereas power may exist without them
Authority is based on physical force, while power is based on consent
Power is permanent, but authority is always temporary
Authority can only be exercised by dictators, while power belongs to citizens
questions.e: Authority is power wrapped in legitimacy; people obey authority because they recognize it as right and proper. Power can be held by a gunman who lacks any moral or institutional backing.
questions.p: Authority na power wey carry legitimacy and respect, so people dey obey am willingly. But power fit dey person hand even if nobody respect am, like armed robber.

questions.q: Legitimacy in government is most accurately defined as the:
o: Total control over the national budget and resources
Ability to suppress opposition parties completely
Acceptance of a government's right to rule by the governed
Establishment of a one-party political system
questions.e: Legitimacy refers to the popular recognition and acceptance of the legality and appropriateness of a particular government or regime to hold power.
questions.p: Legitimacy mean say di citizens accept say di government get right to rule dem. E show say people believe for di system.

questions.q: A military regime that seizes power through a coup d'etat often lacks which of the following initially?
o: Physical control of territory
Constitutional legitimacy
Coercive power
Administrative machinery
questions.e: While a military junta holds immense coercive power and controls state machinery, it lacks constitutional legitimacy because it did not come to power through recognized legal or democratic processes.
questions.p: Even though military government get power and fit use gun make people obey, dem usually no get constitutional legitimacy because dem no follow law enter office.

questions.q: In a unitary state, sovereignty is characterized as being:
o: Concentrated at the central government with supreme legal authority
Divided equally between federal and regional governments
Retained exclusively by traditional rulers
Vested solely in local government councils
questions.e: Sovereignty in a unitary system is centralized. The central government holds supreme power and can create or abolish lower levels of government at will.
questions.p: For unitary system, sovereignty dey concentrated for center. Na di central government get supreme power to do anything and fit even cancel regional or local governments.

questions.q: Which type of democracy is best suited for a modern nation-state with a large population like Nigeria?
o: Direct democracy
Plebiscitary democracy
Representative democracy
Autocratic democracy
questions.e: Representative democracy allows citizens to elect officials to make decisions on their behalf, making it practical for large populations where direct participation by everyone is impossible.
questions.p: Because population too plenty for country like Nigeria, direct democracy no go work. Na representative democracy wey we dey vote people to go represent us wey dey best.

questions.q: Legal sovereignty refers to the supreme power to:
o: Overthrow an unpopular government
Enforce laws without any domestic opposition
Control international trade and foreign policy
Make, amend, and repeal laws within a state
questions.e: Legal sovereignty is vested in the body in a state that has the ultimate legal competence to make and unmake laws, such as the parliament or legislature in a constitutional framework.
questions.p: Legal sovereignty na di supreme power wey law give particular body, like parliament, to dey make, change, or cancel laws for country.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental feature of a true democracy?
o: Protection of fundamental human rights and the rule of law
Absence of opposition parties
Appointment of lifelong legislators by the executive
Censorship of all independent media houses
questions.e: A true democracy guarantees citizens fundamental human rights, equality before the law, and adherence to the rule of law, ensuring that government power is limited.
questions.p: True democracy must protect human rights and follow rule of law. E make sure say government power get limit and citizen freedom dey safe.

questions.q: Max Weber categorized authority into three main types. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
o: Charismatic authority
Oligarchic authority
Legal-rational authority
Traditional authority
questions.e: Max Weber classified authority into traditional, charismatic, and legal-rational. Oligarchic is a form of government by a few, not one of Weber's types of authority.
questions.p: Max Weber talk say authority na traditional, charismatic, and legal-rational. Oligarchic no join Weber classification; na type of government where small group dey rule.

questions.q: External sovereignty implies that a sovereign state must:
o: Surrender its defense to international organizations
Depend on neighboring countries for its foreign policy decisions
Be completely free from foreign control or subjection
Adopt a capitalist economic system
questions.e: External sovereignty means a state is independent in international affairs, recognizing no higher authority than itself in its dealings with other nations.
questions.p: External sovereignty mean say country independent for international level. Dem no dey under control of any other country for their foreign policy.

questions.q: A primary danger of absolute majoritarianism in a democracy is that it can lead to:
o: The total elimination of the ruling party
Excessive protection of minority rights
The collapse of the legal system
The tyranny of the majority over minority groups
questions.e: When majority rule is absolute without constitutional safeguards, it can result in the tyranny of the majority, where the interests and rights of minority groups are ignored or suppressed.
questions.p: If majority rule get no check, e fit turn to tyranny of the majority, where those wey plenty for population go begin oppress or neglect rights of minority groups.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a unitary system of government?
o: The legislature and the executive are fused at all levels.
Power is constitutionally shared between the central and regional governments.
Sovereignty resides strictly with the federating units.
All governmental powers are concentrated in a single central authority.
questions.e: In a unitary system of government, all legislative and administrative powers are concentrated at the national or central level. Regional or local governments only exist and exercise power by the grace of the central government.
questions.p: For unitary system, na only one central government get all the power to run the country. If local government get any power, na because the central government give dem.

questions.q: A major distinction between a federal state and a unitary state is that in a federal state,
o: there is no provision for local government administration.
power is constitutionally divided between different levels of government.
the judiciary is completely controlled by the executive arm.
the constitution is supreme over all authorities.
questions.e: Federalism is characterized by the constitutional division of powers between the central government and the component units (such as states or provinces). Neither level is subordinate to the other in its sphere of authority.
questions.p: Weton make federal government different be say, constitution don share power enter two or more levels like federal and state. Nobody go carry another person power by force.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is a classic example of a federation?
o: The French Republic
The United Kingdom
The Federal Republic of Nigeria
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
questions.e: Nigeria operates a federal system of government comprising a central government, 36 state governments, and the Federal Capital Territory, all sharing constitutional powers. The United Kingdom and France are unitary states, while Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy.
questions.p: Nigeria na clear example of country wey dey practice federalism because power dey shared between federal government and the 36 states.

questions.q: A confederal system of government is inherently unstable primarily because
o: the federating units retain their right to secede from the union.
there is no written constitution to guide the member states.
citizens owe direct allegiance to the central authority rather than their states.
the central government has absolute control over the component units.
questions.e: A confederation is a loose association of sovereign states where the central government is very weak. Because member states retain their sovereignty and right of secession, the union is fragile and prone to collapse.
questions.p: Confederal system weak well well because each state still get full power to comot from the union anytime dem like. Because the central government no get strong power, the thing dey scatter easily.

questions.q: In a constitutional monarchy, the head of state typically
o: exercises absolute executive and legislative powers.
is elected directly by the citizens for a fixed tenure.
performs mostly ceremonial duties while real power lies with the elected parliament.
acts as both the head of state and the head of government simultaneously.
questions.e: In a constitutional monarchy like the United Kingdom, the monarch (king or queen) serves as a ceremonial head of state. Executive governance is vested in the prime minister and parliament.
questions.p: For constitutional monarchy, king or queen just dey sit down look as ceremonial head. Na the parliament and prime minister dey hold the real political power.

questions.q: Which of the following defines a republic?
o: A system where the prime minister is appointed by a foreign power.
A state ruled strictly by military dictators who seized power.
A nation governed exclusively by traditional rulers and chiefs.
A country where the head of state is not a monarch and power derives from the people.
questions.e: A republic is a form of government in which political power resides in the people, who elect their representatives and head of state (usually a president), rather than having a hereditary monarch.
questions.p: Republic mean say na citizens dey choose their leader through election, and head of state no be king or queen wey inherit throne.

questions.q: Why is devolution of power a key feature of some unitary states?
o: To convert the unitary state into a full confederation
To eliminate the need for a national legislature
To ease administrative burdens while retaining central supremacy
To grant permanent sovereignty to local authorities
questions.e: Devolution allows a unitary government to delegate certain law-making and administrative functions to regions (such as Scotland in the UK) without surrendering its ultimate legal supremacy over those regions.
questions.p: Even though unitary government get all power, dem fit share small work give regional areas make things easy, but central government still senior everybody.

questions.q: Which of the following is a structural disadvantage of a federal system?
o: It is usually very expensive to run due to duplication of organs of government.
It prevents minority groups from ever voicing their opinions.
It completely eliminates political rivalry between regions and the center.
It encourages rapid decision-making during national emergencies.
questions.e: Federalism is financially demanding because it requires maintaining separate executive, legislative, and judicial structures at both the federal and state levels, leading to high cost of governance.
questions.p: Federal government system cost money die because you go maintain federal level, then go maintain state level separately. Everything double!

questions.q: An absolute monarchy differs from a republic because in an absolute monarchy,
o: the citizens enjoy unlimited fundamental human rights.
political power is acquired through hereditary succession.
elections are conducted transparently every four years.
the ruler is subject to the supreme laws of a written constitution.
questions.e: In an absolute monarchy, power is passed down through royal bloodlines and the monarch wields unchecked authority. In a republic, leadership is based on popular mandate and regular elections.
questions.p: For absolute monarchy, na family lineage dey carry power pass from father to pikin. No election dey happen like for republic.

questions.q: The primary objective of creating federating units in a multinational state is to
o: accommodate ethnic diversity and prevent domination of minorities.
ensure that only one political party wins all elections.
abolish cultural differences among the populace.
centralize the collection of all taxes under one regional head.
questions.e: Federalism provides a framework that brings diverse ethnic or linguistic groups together under one nation while granting them autonomy to manage their local affairs, thereby dousing ethnic tensions.
questions.p: Dem dey use federalism pack different ethnic groups together inside one country, so that small tribes no go feel say big tribes wan swallow dem.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes a confederation from a federation?
o: Federations are always democratic, while confederations are always monarchical.
Confederations possess a powerful central army, unlike federations.
Federations have written constitutions, while confederations do not.
In a federation, citizens owe allegiance directly to the central government, whereas in a confederation, allegiance is primarily to the component units.
questions.e: In a federal state, citizens are subject to both state and federal laws and owe direct loyalty to the federation. In a confederation, the central government lacks direct authority over individual citizens, who only owe allegiance to their respective member states.
questions.p: For federation, citizens obey federal government straight. But for confederation, na your state government you know; central government no get direct power over individual citizens.

questions.q: Which of the following countries operates a unitary system of government?
o: Federal Republic of Nigeria
Republic of Ghana
Canada
United States of America
questions.e: Ghana operates a unitary system of government where power is concentrated in the central government in Accra, with local assemblies acting as administrative units. USA, Nigeria, and Canada are federal states.
questions.p: Ghana na unitary country because their central government for Accra dey call the shots, unlike Nigeria or USA wey be federal state.

questions.q: Which of the following arms of government is primarily vested with the responsibility of making, amending, and repealing laws in a democratic state?
o: The Executive
The Civil Service
The Legislature
The Judiciary
questions.e: The legislature is the principal law-making organ in a democratic system of government. It debates bills and passes them into law for the state.
questions.p: Na legislature be the main arm wey dey make, change, and cancel laws for country.

questions.q: The core doctrine of separation of powers, as propounded by Baron de Montesquieu, aims primarily to achieve which of the following objectives?
o: Ensure absolute power remains with the president
Make the judiciary subordinate to the legislature
Prevent tyranny and protect citizens' liberties
Speed up the execution of government budgets
questions.e: Montesquieu advocated for the separation of powers to prevent tyranny by ensuring that no single organ concentrates absolute authority, thus safeguarding individual freedom.
questions.p: Montesquieu bring separation of powers so that one person or group no go pack all power become dictator and oppress people.

questions.q: Under a presidential system of government, the principle of checks and balances allows the legislature to perform which of the following functions over the executive?
o: Appointing all local government chairmen
Approving ministerial nominees and major budget estimates
Directly commanding the armed forces during wartime
Presiding over all high court sessions
questions.e: In a presidential system, the legislature checks the executive by scrutinizing and approving key political appointments like ministers and the national budget.
questions.p: Under presidential system, law-makers dey use their power check executive by vetting minister nominees and approving money for budget.

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic mechanism through which the executive arm can check the powers of the legislature?
o: Passing a vote of no confidence
Interpreting the constitutionality of laws
Impeachment of the legislature
Vetoing a bill passed by parliament
questions.e: The executive, through the president or governor, exercises a check on the legislature by refusing to sign a bill into law, thereby exercising a veto.
questions.p: Executive fit use veto power reject bill wey parliament don pass, as one way to check their power.

questions.q: The primary function of the judiciary in a democratic federation is to
o: interpret the constitution and settle legal disputes.
conduct general elections and register political parties.
implement public policies formulated by the cabinet.
collect taxes and distribute revenue to states.
questions.e: The judiciary is the third organ of government whose primary duty is to interpret the laws and dispense justice impartially in disputes.
questions.p: Na court work to interpret law and settle wahala between people or different arms of government.

questions.q: An overlapping function where the executive performs a quasi-legislative role is evident when
o: lawmakers debate motion papers on the floor.
ministers issue statutory instruments or subsidiary legislation.
voters elect representatives during general elections.
judges pass judgement on criminal cases.
questions.e: Delegated legislation occurs when the executive is empowered by parliament to make rules and statutory instruments, which is a quasi-legislative function.
questions.p: When ministers or government agencies dey make rules and regulations based on power given by parliament, na quasi-legislative function be that.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'checks and balances'?
o: A situation where the judiciary controls the police and the military
Complete fusion of legislative and executive powers in one cabinet
Total independence of each organ of government without any contact
Constitutional provisions enabling organs to restrain the actions of other organs
questions.e: Checks and balances mean that although powers are separated, each organ is given constitutional means to watch, control, or limit the activities of the other organs.
questions.p: Checks and balances mean say even though powers separate, each organ get power make dem check wetieldem other ones dey do.

questions.q: In a parliamentary system of government, the executive branch is
o: appointed directly by the supreme court justices.
completely independent of parliamentary votes of confidence.
drawn from and accountable to the legislature.
strictly separated from the legislature with distinct membership.
questions.e: Unlike the presidential system, the parliamentary system fuses executive and legislative powers, meaning ministers are members of parliament and answerable to it.
questions.p: For parliamentary system, executive and legislature join body together; na from parliament dem dey pick ministers.

questions.q: If the Nigerian Supreme Court declares a newly enacted act of the National Assembly null and void because it contravenes the constitution, the court is exercising its power of
o: judicial review.
parliamentary immunity.
delegated legislation.
executive veto.
questions.e: Judicial review is the power of the courts to examine laws passed by the legislature or actions taken by the executive and declare them unconstitutional if they violate the supreme law.
questions.p: When court cancel law because e jam constitution, na judicial review dem use.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of a rigid separation of powers, as practiced in a strict presidential system, is that it can lead to
o: unlimited dictatorship by the head of the judiciary.
instantaneous passing of emergency bills without debate.
the total absence of political parties.
deadlock or gridlock between the executive and the legislature.
questions.e: Strict separation of powers creates independent coordinate branches, which often leads to political stalemates or gridlock when the executive and legislature disagree.
questions.p: If separation too tight, e fit cause serious deadlock or fight between president and parliament when dem no agree.

questions.q: Which of the following public officials typically heads the legislative arm at the federal level in Nigeria?
o: The President of the Senate
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation
The Attorney-General of the Federation
questions.e: At the federal level in Nigeria, the National Assembly consists of the Senate and House of Representatives, with the Senate President presiding over the upper chamber.
questions.p: Na Senate President dey head the Senate, wey be part of the national assembly law-making body.

questions.q: The independence of the judiciary is best guaranteed through which of the following measures?
o: Allowing the executive to remove judges at will based on policy disagreements
Ensuring security of tenure and adequate financial autonomy for judges
Making judges answerable to party leaders for their daily rulings
Subjecting judicial appointments to popular public elections every four years
questions.e: Judicial independence thrives when judges enjoy secure tenure (freedom from arbitrary dismissal) and financial autonomy, shielding them from external pressure.
questions.p: If you wan make court dey independent, judges must get job security and their own money make nobody use hunger control dem.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a written constitution?
o: An agreement signed by traditional rulers before independence
A document that is enacted by a military decree without public debate
A single document containing the fundamental laws and rules of a state
A collection of unwritten conventions, traditions, and judicial precedents
questions.e: A written constitution is formally embodied in a single document containing the fundamental laws and principles of a government. It is systematically drafted and ratified at a specific point in time.
questions.p: Written constitution na one single document wey contain all the main laws and rules of how government suppose run. Dem dey write am down for one place so everybody fit see am.

questions.q: An unwritten constitution is primarily characterized by the fact that it
o: cannot be amended under any circumstances by the legislature
consists entirely of uncodified customs, traditions, and acts of parliament
exists only in oral traditions passed down through generations
does not provide for the separation of powers among arms of government
questions.e: An unwritten constitution is not contained in a single document. Instead, its rules are sourced from various uncodified statutes, judicial precedents, historical charters, and political conventions.
questions.p: Unwritten constitution no mean say dem no dey write anything down at all; e just mean say the laws no dey inside one single book. E come from different old customs, court judgments, and parliament laws.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a primary material source of a constitution?
o: Daily newspaper editorials and political blogs
Historical historical textbooks written by foreign authors
Manifestos of opposition political parties during elections
Judicial precedents and previous landmark court rulings
questions.e: Judicial precedents (case law) form a crucial source of constitutional law because interpretations given by apex courts shape how constitutional provisions are applied.
questions.p: Court judgments and previous high court rulings na major source of constitution because how judges interpret law dey help shape how government dey use the constitution.

questions.q: A rigid constitution is one that
o: can be suspended instantly whenever a state of emergency is declared
prohibits any form of amendment by the elected national assembly
can only be amended through a special, complex, and cumbersome legislative procedure
requires the unanimous consent of all citizens before any clause is altered
questions.e: A rigid constitution requires a special, difficult amending process, often involving referendums or special majorities, to safeguard its provisions from arbitrary political changes.
questions.p: Rigid constitution hard to amend because e need special and heavy process, like getting two-thirds majority or conducting referendum, before dem fit change anything inside.

questions.q: What distinguishes a flexible constitution from a rigid one?
o: A flexible constitution can be amended through the ordinary legislative law-making process
A flexible constitution cannot be interpreted by the supreme court
A flexible constitution applies only to unitary forms of government
A flexible constitution is always unwritten and purely based on conventions
questions.e: The key feature of a flexible constitution is that it can be amended by the parliament using the same simple majority procedure used for passing ordinary laws.
questions.p: Flexible constitution easy to amend because parliament fit change am using ordinary law-making process without any special hard conditions.

questions.q: In a federal state like Nigeria, why is a rigid written constitution considered practically mandatory?
o: To protect the constituent regions or states from being dominated by the central government
To ensure that the president holds executive power without legislative interference
To prevent the central government from borrowing money from international banks
To eliminate the need for an independent judiciary and Supreme Court
questions.e: Federalism involves a division of powers between the centre and component units. A rigid written constitution prevents the central government from unilaterally altering this power-sharing arrangement.
questions.p: For federal country like Nigeria, rigid written constitution important so that federal government no go just wake up and change power-sharing formula to cheat the state governments.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a unitary constitution?
o: A constitution that is exclusively unwritten and based on parliamentary supremacy
A constitution that does not recognize fundamental human rights of citizens
A constitution that divides power equally between regional and local councils
A constitution where all governmental powers are concentrated in a single central authority
questions.e: A unitary constitution establishes a system where ultimate political power rests with the central government, which may delegate administrative duties to lower units but retains supreme authority.
questions.p: Unitary constitution na system where all government power gather for one central authority. Even if dem share work give local areas, na central government still get final say.

questions.q: Conventions as a source of constitutional law refer to
o: rulings delivered by customary court judges in rural communities
unwritten political rules and practices that are widely accepted and observed
formal laws enacted by the legislature during a state of emergency
international treaties signed between sovereign African nations
questions.e: Constitutional conventions are unwritten political habits, maxims, and practices that lack legal enforceability in court but are strictly followed by convention in governance.
questions.p: Conventions na those unwritten rules and old political habits wey everybody dey respect and follow for government work, even though court no fit jail anybody for breaking dem.

questions.q: Which of the following documents historically serves as a vital source of constitutional development in Nigeria?
o: The 1914 Amalgamation Report by Lord Lugard
The African Union Constitutive Act of 2002
The 1922 Clifford Constitution
The United Nations Charter on Human Rights
questions.e: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is historically significant as the first constitution that introduced elective principle into the legislative council in Nigeria.
questions.p: The 1922 Clifford Constitution na important historical source for Nigeria because naim introduce election for the very first time inside our legislative council.

questions.q: An autochthonous constitution is best described as one that
o: is imposed on a colony by the departing colonial imperial power
originates natively from the people of the country and has indigenous roots
applies strictly to monarchical systems of government without a parliament
can only be amended by an external international tribunal
questions.e: An autochthonous constitution is home-grown; it derives its ultimate legal authority and legitimacy from the indigenous people of the state rather than from an imperial power.
questions.p: Autochthonous constitution na home-grown constitution. E mean say na the citizens of the country produce am themselves, and e no come from any colonial master authority.

questions.q: What is the primary danger associated with an excessively rigid constitution?
o: It increases the cost of conducting national population censuses
It automatically turns a democratic state into a totalitarian dictatorship
It encourages frequent military coups due to an inability to adapt to changing societal needs
It prevents the judiciary from interpreting any criminal laws
questions.e: When a constitution is too rigid, society cannot legally and peacefully reform outdated laws, which can lead to social unrest, political deadlock, and extra-constitutional overthrows.
questions.p: If constitution too rigid, society no go fit change laws when things change. This kind frustration fit cause political crisis or make military people use force enter power.

questions.q: Which of the following sources of a constitution possesses the highest legal authority in a democratic nation?
o: The supreme constitutional document of the land
Acts passed by the national legislature
Bye-laws made by local government councils
Executive orders issued by the president
questions.e: The constitution itself is the fundamental and supreme law of the land; any other law, act, or bye-law that contradicts it is null and void to the extent of its inconsistency.
questions.p: The constitution na the highest law of the land. Any other law, act, or order wey go conflict with am na waste time because constitution na baba pass.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most fundamental feature of the Rule of Law as espoused by A.V. Dicey?
o: Absolute power of the military government
Immunity of public officials from all forms of prosecution
Supremacy of the legislature over the judiciary
Equality before the law and absence of arbitrary power
questions.e: Dicey's doctrine emphasizes that no person is above the law and everyone is subject to the ordinary law of the land administered by normal courts.
questions.p: Na Dicey talk say nobody too big pass law and government no suppose punish person anyhow without court trial.

questions.q: In a democratic state, fundamental human rights are best described as:
o: Privileges granted temporarily by the ruling political party
Conditional rewards given only to loyal tax-paying citizens
Gifts distributed by the executive branch during election periods
Inherent entitlements that belong to every individual by virtue of being human
questions.e: Fundamental human rights are universal, inherent, and inalienable rights possessed by all human beings regardless of nationality or status.
questions.p: Human rights na those natural things wey belong to everybody just because you be human being, no be gift from government.

questions.q: Which body is constitutionally empowered in Nigeria to handle cases of fundamental human rights abuses?
o: The National Youth Service Corps Directorate
The State House of Assembly
The High Court
The Local Government Council
questions.e: Under the Nigerian Constitution, the Federal or State High Court has the primary original jurisdiction to enforce fundamental human rights.
questions.p: Na High Court get power for Nigeria to protect people when their human rights don break or when police maltreat them.

questions.q: A major limitation to the absolute enjoyment of fundamental human rights in Nigeria is:
o: The interests of public defense, public safety, and public order
The doctrine of collective bargaining
The rotational presidency agreement
The annual national budget allocation
questions.e: No right is absolute; rights can be legally restricted by the government to protect public safety, health, and the rights of other citizens.
questions.p: No right dey wey be say you must do am by fire by force; government fit restrict am small to protect peace and safety for everybody.

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios is a direct violation of the Rule of Law?
o: Passing a bill through the legislature after public hearings
Detaining a political opponent indefinitely without trial
Prosecuting a corrupt official in a competent court
Arresting a suspect with a valid court warrant
questions.e: Indefinite detention without trial goes against personal liberty and the principle of regular legal procedures.
questions.p: To lock person up for cell for long time without carrying am go court na clear violation of rule of law.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of writing a writ of Habeas Corpus?
o: To request a reduction in commercial tax rates
To demand an immediate dissolution of parliament
To compel the president to assent to a constitutional amendment
To challenge an unlawful detention and compel the authorities to produce the suspect in court
questions.e: Habeas corpus is a judicial remedy designed to protect individuals against illegal imprisonment by forcing authorities to bring the detained person before a judge.
questions.p: Habeas corpus na court order wey dey force security agents make dem bring person wey dem arrest go court make judge see weda na lawful arrest.

questions.q: Which of these institutions acts as a watchdog to protect citizens from administrative injustice and abuse of power in Nigeria?
o: The Public Complaints Commission (Ombudsman)
The Federal Road Safety Corps
The Central Bank of Nigeria
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company
questions.e: The Ombudsman or Public Complaints Commission investigates complaints from citizens regarding administrative injustices and bureaucratic high-handedness.
questions.p: Na Ombudsman (Public Complaints Commission) dey help citizens fight government workers or agencies when dem treat them anyhow.

questions.q: The concept of 'administrative tribunals' sometimes conflicts with the Rule of Law because they:
o: Function exclusively to collect local government rates
May bypass normal judicial processes and limit the right of appeal to ordinary courts
Always consist of military generals
Operate entirely outside any legal framework
questions.e: Administrative tribunals handle specialized disputes quickly, but if they deny fair hearing or judicial review, they undermine Dicey's principle of ordinary legal administration.
questions.p: Sometimes administrative panels dey shake rule of law because dem fit bypass normal court process and deny people proper appeal.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, fundamental human rights are contained in:
o: Chapter VII
Chapter I
Chapter IV
Chapter II
questions.e: Chapter IV of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution (Sections 33 to 46) explicitly outlines the fundamental rights of citizens.
questions.p: Na Chapter IV of our 1999 Constitution contain all those rights like right to life, dignity, and freedom of movement.

questions.q: Which of the following best guarantees the independence of the judiciary, a key pillar of the Rule of Law?
o: Appointment of judges by the ruling party executive without screening
Removing judges whenever they give judgments against the government
Security of tenure and financial autonomy for judicial officers
Subjecting judicial verdicts to approval by the national assembly
questions.e: Judges can only act impartially if their jobs are secure and their budgets do not depend on the whims of the executive arm.
questions.p: Make court independent mean say judge job secure and money dey flow well so dem no go dey fear anybody before dem give judgment.

questions.q: An example of a civic obligation that complements the enjoyment of human rights is:
o: Destroying public property during peaceful protests
Obeying lawful orders and respecting the rights of others
Disobeying traffic regulations
Evading the payment of income tax
questions.e: Rights come with responsibilities; citizens must respect the law and the rights of their fellow countrymen.
questions.p: As you get your own rights, na duty make you obey law and respect other people own too.

questions.q: Prerogative writs such as Mandamus, Certiorari, and Prohibition are primarily utilized by the judiciary to:
o: Control administrative excess and ensure lower bodies act within legal bounds
Create new laws when the legislature is on recess
Appoint ministers and board chairmen
Collect revenue for the federation account
questions.e: Prerogative orders are judicial instruments used by superior courts to supervise lower courts, tribunals, and public officers to prevent abuse of power.
questions.p: Na court instruments be these ones wey higher court take dey check lower court or government agencies make dem no abuse power.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of a political party in a democratic state?
o: Monitoring the judicial arm to ensure fair interpretation of laws
Mobilizing citizens exclusively for revenue generation and tax compliance
Influencing specific government policies without contesting elections
Capturing and exercising political power through constitutional means
questions.e: Unlike pressure groups that seek to influence policy, the fundamental goal of a political party is to win elections and form government. Through this, they implement their manifestos and direct state affairs.
questions.p: Unlike pressure groups wey dey find how to beg government, party main work na make dem win election and enter power so that dem go fit run government according to their manifesto.

questions.q: A political party system characterized by the existence of only two dominant parties with equal or near-equal electoral strength is known as a:
o: Two-party system
Multi-party system
Zero-party system
One-party system
questions.e: A two-party system features two major political parties that regularly alternate in power, as seen historically in the United States. It limits voters to two main viable choices at the polls.
questions.p: Two-party system na when only two major parties dey strong well-well inside country, and power dey alternate between dem like wetin we dey see for America.

questions.q: An association of like-minded individuals organized to influence government policies and decisions without necessarily fielding candidates for elections is called a:
o: Factions council
Constituency assembly
Pressure group
Political party
questions.e: Pressure groups or interest groups focus on promoting specific sectional or public interests by lobbying decision-makers instead of seeking direct political offices.
questions.p: Pressure group na association of people wey carry same mindset come together to pressure government make dem do wetin dem want, but dem no dey contest election to become president or governor.

questions.q: Which of the following tactics is most commonly and effectively employed by trade unions as a pressure group to press home their demands?
o: Issuing direct executive orders to dissolve the national assembly
Embarking on industrial strikes and peaceful boycotts
Filing treason charges against uncooperative cabinet ministers
Contesting local government elections under a unified banner
questions.e: Trade unions protect workers' rights primarily by withdrawing their labour through strikes or threatening industrial action to compel employers or the government to negotiate.
questions.p: Trade unions like NLC dey use strike action or protest to force government or employers make dem agree to their demands when negotiation fail.

questions.q: In a multi-party system, coalition governments often become necessary when:
o: The electoral commission bans all opposition parties from campaigning
The military takes over power and suspends the constitution
A single party wins a landslide victory in all legislative constituencies
No single party secures an absolute majority of seats in the legislature
questions.e: When election results produce a hung parliament where no party has the required majority to form a government independently, two or more parties must form a coalition.
questions.p: Coalition government dey happen when election result scatter and no single party fit get clear majority, so two or more parties must join hands to form government.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of a one-party system of government is that it:
o: Denies the electorate a viable alternative choice of leadership
Promotes excessive political instability through frequent coups
Encourages unhealthy competition and wasteful election spending
Guarantees that all minority views are strictly protected by law
questions.e: A one-party state restricts political competition, effectively removing the mechanism for peaceful democratic change of leadership and undermining citizens' freedom of choice.
questions.p: One-party system bad because e no allow citizens choose another person if dem tired of the current ruling party, which fit lead to dictatorship.

questions.q: What distinguishes an anomic pressure group from an institutional or associational pressure group?
o: It is officially registered and funded by the federal electoral commission
It relies on spontaneous, unstructured, and often violent forms of action
It operates strictly in accordance with international diplomatic protocols
It has a permanent secretariat and a well-defined constitution
questions.e: Anomic interest groups arise spontaneously during crises, such as sudden riots or mob actions, lacking formal organization, rules, or permanent structures.
questions.p: Anomic pressure group na those ones wey just scatter enter street suddenly out of anger, like riot or mob action, because dem no get formal structure or office.

questions.q: An institutional pressure group is best exemplified by an association formed by:
o: Militant youths agitating for resource control in the creeks
University professors and academic staff within the public service
Civil servants and military personnel acting within government bodies
Market women selling food items in an urban open-air market
questions.e: Institutional pressure groups are part of the machinery of government, such as the civil service, armed forces, or church hierarchies, which attempt to influence policy from within.
questions.p: Institutional pressure group na those groups wey belong inside government setup itself, like military officers or civil servants wey dey try influence policy from within.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why elite-backed pressure groups often wield enormous influence over public policy in developing democracies?
o: They command millions of foot soldiers who can violently overthrow the state
They are constitutionally mandated to vet all bills passed by the national legislature
They represent the poorest segments of the rural agrarian population
They possess superior financial resources, technical expertise, and direct access to decision-makers
questions.e: Elite pressure groups leverage their wealth, professional expertise, and personal connections with political leaders to lobby effectively for policies favourable to their interests.
questions.p: Elite pressure group dey get power because dem get money, connections, and brain to lobby government officials easily pass ordinary citizens.

questions.q: The process through which political parties select their candidates to contest in a general election is referred to as:
o: Electoral delimitation
Referendum balloting
Primary election
Legislative ratification
questions.e: Party primaries are internal elections or selection processes where registered party members choose who will represent the party as their flagbearer in the main election.
questions.p: Primary election na the internal contest where party members vote to choose the exact person wey go carry party flag for main general election.

questions.q: Which of the following functions is performed by political parties in bridging the gap between the government and the governed?
o: Collecting taxes and managing the foreign reserves
Political education and mobilization of the electorate
Enacting criminal legislation and sentencing offenders
Adjudicating disputes arising from commercial contracts
questions.e: Political parties educate citizens on public issues, explain government policies, and encourage active participation in the political process, acting as a link between rulers and citizens.
questions.p: Political parties dey help educate citizens about wetin government dey do and make sure say people understand political matters well-well.

questions.q: An association that promotes the interests of a specific economic sector, such as the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), is classified as a:
o: Rebel guerrilla movement
Anomic pressure group
Promotional pressure group
Economic or sectional pressure group
questions.e: Sectional or economic pressure groups protect the specific material and financial interests of their members, such as trade unions, chambers of commerce, and manufacturers associations.
questions.p: Sectional pressure group na group wey dey look after the business and economic interest of their members, like manufacturers or bankers association.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies is empowered by the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended) to register political parties?
o: The Independent National Electoral Commission
The National Orientation Agency
The Code of Conduct Bureau
The National Judicial Council
questions.e: INEC is the sole statutory body established by the Nigerian constitution to register political parties, monitor their activities, and regulate their finances.
questions.p: Na INEC get power according to the law to register political party and check how dem dey run am for Nigeria.

questions.q: In an electoral system where seats are allocated strictly in proportion to the total votes cast for a party, this is best described as
o: absolute majority system
alternative vote
proportional representation
first-past-the-post
questions.e: Proportional representation ensures that the percentage of seats a party wins in the legislature matches closely with the percentage of total votes it received in the election.
questions.p: Proportional representation mean say weda party win small or big, the seat dem go get for parliament go follow the percentage of votes wey dem pack.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a returning officer at a federal constituency collation centre during a general election in Nigeria?
o: To announce and declare the final election results for the constituency
To arrest electoral offenders at the voting centres
To accredit eligible voters before ballot casting begins
To distribute sensitive electoral materials to polling units
questions.e: A returning officer is responsible for collating results from various wards and officially declaring the winner for that specific constituency.
questions.p: Returning officer work na to gather all the result from different wards come announce winner for that constituency.

questions.q: An electoral system that divides a country into single-member constituencies where the candidate with the highest number of votes wins, regardless of an absolute majority, is known as
o: Indirect election system
Plurality system
List system
Second ballot system
questions.e: The plurality system, also called first-past-the-post, requires only a relative majority (highest votes), not necessarily over 50 percent.
questions.p: Plurality system, wey people sabi as first-past-the-post, just need make person get highest vote pass everybody, even if e no reach half.

questions.q: Which of the following is an independent revenue source or financial arrangement designed to guarantee the autonomy of INEC in Nigeria?
o: Levying direct taxes on registered political parties
Receiving conditional grants from foreign non-governmental organisations
Generating funds through the sale of voter cards to citizens
Direct funding through the Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation
questions.e: To maintain neutrality and independence, INEC's funds are charged directly upon the Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation so the executive cannot starve it of money.
questions.p: To make sure say INEC dey independent, their money dey come straight from Consolidated Revenue Fund so federal government no go fit use money hold dem ransom.

questions.q: By-elections are conducted in Nigeria primarily to
o: resolve ties in a gubernatorial run-off election
fill a legislative vacancy caused by death, resignation, or recall
elect a new President when the incumbent travels abroad
test the popularity of newly registered political parties
questions.e: A by-election is a special election held between general elections specifically to fill a vacant seat in a legislative house.
questions.p: Dem dey do by-election when person wey hold political seat die, resign, or dem remove am, so person go replace am sharp sharp.

questions.q: Which of the following features best distinguishes a secret ballot system from an open ballot system?
o: Election results are announced immediately at the polling booth
Voters queue publicly behind the photograph of their preferred candidate
Traditional rulers openly direct their subjects on who to vote for
Voters cast their votes in absolute privacy without anyone knowing their choice
questions.e: The secret ballot ensures voter privacy, protecting citizens from intimidation and coercion during elections.
questions.p: Secret ballot make sure say nobody know who you vote for, so nobody go fit harass or threat you because of your choice.

questions.q: An electoral process where voters rank candidates in order of preference rather than choosing only one is called
o: Preferential voting
Cumulative voting
Open ballot
Block voting
questions.e: Preferential voting allows electors to rank candidates as first, second, third, and so on, which helps reach a majority through redistribution of preferences.
questions.p: Preferential voting mean say voter go arrange candidate starting from the one wey e like pass down to the least.

questions.q: What is the constitutional implication if a presidential candidate in Nigeria wins the highest number of votes but fails to secure at least 25% of the votes in two-thirds of the states and the Federal Capital Territory?
o: The election is cancelled and postponed for one year
The runner-up is sworn in as the substantive president
A run-off election is conducted between the top two candidates
The candidate is automatically declared winner after seven days
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution mandates that aside from scoring the highest votes, a presidential winner must meet the geographical spread requirement of 25% in at least 24 states plus the FCT, failing which a run-off is held.
questions.p: If presidential candidate win highest vote but fail to get 25 percent for two-third of states plus Abuja, constitution talk say another election (run-off) must happen.

questions.q: The delimitation of electoral constituencies in Nigeria is the statutory responsibility of
o: The National Population Commission
The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
The National Boundary Commission
The Independent National Electoral Commission
questions.e: INEC has the constitutional power to divide the country into federal constituencies and senatorial districts for election purposes.
questions.p: Na INEC get constitutional duty to share the country into different constituencies and senatorial districts for election.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of electronic voting and collation over manual systems?
o: It reduces human error and speeds up result transmission
It completely eliminates the need for security personnel
It guarantees that all registered citizens will vote
It removes the need for civic education
questions.e: Electronic transmission of results helps curb ballot box snatching en route to collation centres and speeds up the announcement process.
questions.p: Electronic voting dey help reduce mistake of manual counting and make transmission of result fast well well.

questions.q: Which electoral body in Nigeria is specifically responsible for conducting local government council elections across the states?
o: The Federal Electoral Commission
The Local Government Service Commission
The State Independent Electoral Commission
The Independent National Electoral Commission
questions.e: While INEC conducts federal and state elections, each state has a State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) set up for local government elections.
questions.p: Na State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) dey conduct local government election for each state, no be INEC.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes political socialisation?
o: The legal procedure for registering a new political party in Nigeria
The process by which an individual acquires political values and beliefs
The systematic suppression of opposition voices by the ruling party
The voting pattern observed during general elections
questions.e: Political socialisation is the lifelong process through which people learn and acquire political values, beliefs, and orientations from their environment. Agents like family, school, and media play a key role in shaping this awareness.
questions.p: Na the process wey person take dey learn political belle and belief from im environment, like family and school.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognized legal means of acquiring citizenship in Nigeria?
o: Citizenship by nationalization
Citizenship by registration
Citizenship by birth
Citizenship by naturalization
questions.e: According to the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, citizenship can be acquired by birth, registration, or naturalization. Nationalization refers to the takeover of private businesses by the state, not a way to get citizenship.
questions.p: According to Nigeria constitution, person fit get citizenship through birth, registration, or naturalization. Nationalization na government takeover of private business, no be way to get citizenship.

questions.q: Public opinion can be effectively measured through which of the following methods?
o: Secret meetings of traditional rulers
Public opinion polls and scientific surveys
Editorial directives from government-owned newspapers
Random speculation by political party thugs
questions.e: Scientific opinion polls and surveys use statistical methods to gather representative views from the population. This makes them the most reliable tool for measuring public opinion.
questions.p: Na through scientific survey and opinion poll people dey use measurewet wetin public dey think well well.

questions.q: Dual citizenship is permitted in Nigeria for:
o: Persons holding political office in the executive arm
Only citizens by naturalization
All citizens regardless of how citizenship was acquired
Any citizen by birth
questions.e: The Nigerian constitution allows citizens by birth to hold dual citizenship. However, citizens by registration or naturalization may forfeit their Nigerian citizenship if they acquire another country's citizenship.
questions.p: Nigeria constitution allow person wey dem born for Nigeria to hold two citizenship. But if na registration or naturalization you take get am, e fit scatter if you carry another country passport.

questions.q: Which agent of political socialisation is usually considered the most influential during early childhood?
o: Trade unions
The mass media
The family
The electoral commission
questions.e: The family is the primary and most influential agent of political socialisation because children are first exposed to authority, values, and attitudes within the home.
questions.p: Family na the number one agent wey dey shape pikin political mindset because na house dem take start to dey see authority and values.

questions.q: An active citizen in a democracy is expected to:
o: Support any policy introduced by the ruling party without questioning
Constructively engage in civic duties and hold leaders accountable
Pay taxes only when threatened by law enforcement agents
Remain completely indifferent to government policies
questions.e: An active citizen participates in governance, obeys the law, pays taxes, and holds elected officials accountable. Indifference or blind loyalty weakens democratic institutions.
questions.p: Active citizen suppose perform im civic duty, pay tax, and make sure say government dey accountable. No be to just sit down look or follow anyhow.

questions.q: The voluntary expression of views and attitudes held by a significant portion of the public on an issue of public concern is known as:
o: Public service
Public enterprise
Public opinion
Public execution
questions.e: Public opinion represents the collective preferences, attitudes, and views of a population regarding contemporary public issues and government policies.
questions.p: Public opinion na the general view and feeling wey people carry for head concerning matter wey affect everybody.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions can lead to the deprivation of Nigerian citizenship for a naturalized citizen?
o: Traveling out of the country for more than one year
Criticizing a local government chairman in the newspaper
Failure to vote in a presidential election
Disloyalty to the Federal Republic of Nigeria
questions.e: A naturalized citizen can be deprived of their Nigerian citizenship by the president if they are shown to be disloyal, trade with an enemy country during war, or are imprisoned for a serious criminal offense within a few years of naturalization.
questions.p: Dem fit collect citizenship from person wey naturalize if e show disloyalty to Nigeria or commit grave crime within short time after e collect am.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the mass media is a powerful tool for political socialisation?
o: It reaches a wide audience simultaneously and shapes public agenda
It directly funds political parties during campaigns
It replaces the judicial system in settling disputes
It legally enforces government policies on the citizens
questions.e: The mass media reaches massive numbers of people instantly, making it a powerful vehicle for disseminating information, shaping opinions, and setting the political agenda.
questions.p: Mass media get power because e dey reach millions of people sharp sharp and e dey help shape wetin people dey talk and think about governance.

questions.q: A foreigner wishing to become a Nigerian citizen through registration must satisfy the statutory requirement of:
o: Donating half of their wealth to charity organizations in Abuja
Marrying a serving senator or member of the House of Representatives
Showing clear intention to be domiciled in Nigeria and being of good character
Contesting and winning a local government chairmanship election
questions.e: To acquire Nigerian citizenship by registration, an applicant must be of good character, show a clear intention to reside permanently in Nigeria, and meet other constitutional provisions.
questions.p: If foreigner wan register for Nigerian citizenship, e must be person of good character and show say e really wan stay Nigeria permanently.

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates political apathy among citizens?
o: Refusing to collect permanent voter cards and boycotting all elections out of indifference
Organizing peaceful protests against an increase in electricity tariffs
Joining a pressure group to lobby lawmakers for better roads
Writing critical essays about government policies on social media platforms
questions.e: Political apathy refers to a lack of interest, concern, or participation in political and civic activities, such as voting and taking part in elections.
questions.p: Political apathy na when person no send politics at all, like when dem refuse to collect PVC or vote for election because dem no care.

questions.q: An official of the Nigerian civil service who is accused of professional misconduct must be disciplined through procedures established by the:
o: National Judicial Council
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission
National Assembly
Federal Civil Service Commission
questions.e: The Federal Civil Service Commission is the constitutional body responsible for the appointment, promotion, and disciplinary control of civil servants in Nigeria.
questions.p: Na Federal Civil Service Commission get power to employ, promote, and punish any worker wey do wrong inside civil service.

questions.q: The principle of anonymity in the civil service implies that civil servants:
o: Do not sign official documents
Must remain politically neutral at all times
Take neither the credit nor the blame for government policies
Are not allowed to reveal their names to the public
questions.e: Anonymity means civil servants work behind the scenes and ministers take the public praise or condemnation for policy outcomes, protecting the servants from public exposure.
questions.p: Anonymity mean say worker dey work for backend, na the minister dey carry the glory or the blame for any policy, make people no know the worker face.

questions.q: Public corporations are established primarily to:
o: Generate maximum revenue for political party campaigns
Provide essential social services on a commercial or semi-commercial basis
Handle diplomatic relations with foreign nations
Advise the executive arm on legal matters
questions.e: Public corporations (statutory corporations) are set up by acts of parliament to provide vital services like electricity, water, and transport, often combining social service with commercial viability.
questions.p: Dem dey create public corporation to provide important service like light, water, and transport for citizens, and sometimes make small profit too.

questions.q: Red tape in the Nigerian civil service is best defined as:
o: Excessive adherence to rigid rules and bureaucratic delays
The strict separation of duties between junior and senior staff
The process of auditing government accounts annually
The official uniform worn by senior administrative officers
questions.e: Red tape refers to the complex rules, paperwork, and bureaucratic bottlenecks that often delay decision-making and the execution of government business.
questions.p: Red tape na when too many rules, long protocol, and unnecessary paperwork dey delay work make things slow down.

questions.q: A major challenge facing public corporations in Nigeria is:
o: Refusal of citizens to use their services
Complete absence of government funding
Lack of any legal framework establishing them
Excessive government interference and political instability
questions.e: Political interference, frequent changes in management, and corruption often cripple the efficiency and profitability of public corporations in Nigeria.
questions.p: Politicians too dey put mouth for their management, and corruption dey scatter the way corporation suppose dey run well.

questions.q: The permanent secretary in a Nigerian ministry is legally and administratively responsible for:
o: Formulating partisan political manifestoes for the ruling party
Acting as the chief accounting officer of the ministry
Representing Nigeria in international peace talks abroad
Financing the electoral campaigns of the minister
questions.e: The permanent secretary is the administrative head and the chief accounting officer who oversees the day-to-day spending and implementation of policies in the ministry.
questions.p: Permanent secretary na him be the administrative head and chief accounting officer wey dey manage money and daily work inside ministry.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies is responsible for fixing the salaries and wages of civil servants in Nigeria?
o: Central Bank of Nigeria
Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission
Federal Inland Revenue Service
questions.e: The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission is the statutory body tasked with determining and recommending fair salary structures for public servants in Nigeria.
questions.p: Na National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission dey calculate and recommend salary structure for government workers.

questions.q: The neutrality of the civil service means that civil servants:
o: Must serve any political party in power with equal dedication
Are forbidden from voting during general elections
Do not pay personal income tax to the government
Must not belong to any religious organization
questions.e: Neutrality requires civil servants to remain non-partisan so that they can faithfully implement the policies of whichever political party wins democratic elections.
questions.p: Neutrality mean say worker no suppose join politics; any party wey win election, na him work you go loyal to do well.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of a public corporation?
o: It is funded entirely by private shareholders
Its staff are strictly subject to civil service rules
It cannot sue or be sued in a court of law
It has a distinct legal personality separate from the government
questions.e: A public corporation is a body corporate, meaning it can sue, be sued, and hold property in its own name, unlike a regular civil service ministry.
questions.p: Public corporation get him own separate legal identity, meaning e fit sue person or person fit sue am for court, unlike ministry.

questions.q: The transfer of ownership and control of public enterprises to private investors in Nigeria is known as:
o: Commercialization
Privatization
Nationalization
Indigenization
questions.e: Privatization involves selling government-owned enterprises to private individuals or corporate bodies to improve efficiency and reduce waste.
questions.p: Privatization na when government sell him company give private people make business run beta and stop waste.

questions.q: Civil service neutrality is mostly threatened by:
o: Regular payment of worker salaries
Transparent promotion interviews
Political partisanship and godfatherism
Strict adherence to official gazettes
questions.e: When politicians demand loyalty to party rather than the state, or when jobs are secured through political connections (godfatherism), civil service neutrality is compromised.
questions.p: When politicians start to force workers to do party work or use godfatherism to give job, civil service neutrality go spoil.

questions.q: Which of the following pre-colonial Nigerian political systems was predominantly acephalous?
o: The Benin kingdom
The Oyo empire
The Hausa-Fulani emirate
The Igbo traditional system
questions.e: The Igbo political system lacked a central king or paramount ruler, making it acephalous or headless. Power was decentralised among age grades, titled men, and family heads.
questions.p: Igbo political system no get king or central ruler at all, na why dem dey call am acephalous. Authority scatter give age grades, titled men, and family heads.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani administration, the official responsible for the prison and the execution of court sentences was the
o: Galadima
Sarki fada
Yari
Maari
questions.e: The Yari was the chief of prisons and the official in charge of executing capital punishments ordered by the Alkali courts in the Emirate system.
questions.p: Na Yari dem dey give work to look after prison and make sure say judgment wey Alkali court give naim dem carry out.

questions.q: The ultimate check on the tyrannical rule of the Alaafin in the old Oyo empire was the
o: presentation of the calabash of destruction
veto power of the Ogboni cult
banishment by the Bashorun
intervention of the provincial governors
questions.e: When the Alaafin lost the confidence of the Oyomesi, the Bashorun presented him with an empty calabash or parrot's eggs, which signified an order to commit ritual suicide.
questions.p: If Alaafin begin act like tyrant, Bashorun and Oyomesi go send am empty calabash or parrot egg. Dat one na sign say make im drink poison and die.

questions.q: Which body served as the supreme legislative and judicial council in the traditional Igbo political organization?
o: The Age grade council
The Oha-na-eze assembly
The Umuada association
The Oracle priests
questions.e: The village assembly, known as Oha-na-eze or assembly of all male citizens, was the highest decision-making body where laws were made and major disputes were settled.
questions.p: Na the Oha-na-eze village assembly be the highest place where all free men dey gather make law and settle serious matter for Igbo land.

questions.q: The Sokoto caliphate was established primarily as a result of
o: the 1804 Islamic jihad led by Uthman dan Fodio
the treaty signed between the Hausa kings and Fulani scholars
the British conquest of Northern Nigeria
the collapse of the Kanem-Bornu empire
questions.e: Uthman dan Fodio led the 1804 jihad which overthrew the Habe kingdoms and replaced them with the centralised Sokoto Caliphate.
questions.p: Na Uthman dan Fodio lead the 1804 jihad wey remove all the Habe kings and put Sokoto Caliphate for ground.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Yoruba administration, the Aremo was the
o: prime minister and head of the Oyomesi
commander-in-chief of the army
chief priest of Sango
crown prince who was traditionally forbidden from succeeding his father
questions.e: The Aremo was the eldest son of the Alaafin. Due to the fear that he might usurp power, tradition demanded that he commits suicide upon his father's death.
questions.p: Aremo na the first born son of Alaafin. Dem custom no allow am make im inherit throne after im papa die, instead im suppose die follow papa.

questions.q: Which of the following offices in the Hausa-Fulani system performed the duties of a modern minister of finance?
o: Madawaki
Maaji
Waziri
Sarkin Dogarai
questions.e: The Maaji was the treasurer of the emirate, keeping custody of all revenues collected from taxes like zakat, jizya, and jangali.
questions.p: Na Maaji dey keep all the money and wealth for emirate treasury, just like modern minister of finance.

questions.q: A key feature of the pre-colonial Igbo political system was
o: hereditary monarchy
absolute dictatorship
gerontocracy and segmentary lineage
centralised federalism
questions.e: The Igbo system relied heavily on rule by elders (gerontocracy) and autonomous kinship groups (segmentary lineage) rather than a central king.
questions.p: Igbo political system like make old people rule (gerontocracy) and make family units stand on their own instead of one person control everybody.

questions.q: The Alaafin of Oyo was constitutionally expected to rule in conjunction with
o: the Kankanfo
the Ogboni cult
the Oyomesi
the Are Ona Kakanfo
questions.e: The Oyomesi, led by the Bashorun, were the kingmakers and council of state that shared executive and legislative powers with the Alaafin.
questions.p: Na the Oyomesi council naim suppose join hand with Alaafin dey run government and make laws for Oyo empire.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial administration of the Hausa states, the Emirate system was divided into districts, each headed by a
o: Hakimi
Sarkin Fada
Dogari
Alkali
questions.e: An Emirate was decentralised into districts, and the Emir appointed district heads known as Hakimi to collect taxes and maintain order on his behalf.
questions.p: Emir dey share land into small districts, and im go put person wey dem dey call Hakimi make im supervise am and pack tax.

questions.q: The role of the Ogboni society in the old Oyo Empire was mainly to
o: supervise the coronation of new chiefs
act as a mediator between the Alaafin and the Oyomesi
lead the army into foreign wars
collect tolls and market levies
questions.e: The Ogboni cult, an influential earth-worship and judicial body, acted as a constitutional check and balance by mediating political crises between the Alaafin and the Oyomesi.
questions.p: Ogboni group na like peace-maker. If Alaafin and Oyomesi fight, na dem dey enter middle to settle matter and balance power.

questions.q: Democracy is often said to have existed in traditional Igbo society because of the practice of
o: secret ballot voting
equal representation of women in council
universal adult suffrage
open discussion and consensus in village assemblies
questions.e: Decisions in traditional Igbo assemblies were reached through open debates where every free citizen had a voice until a consensus was achieved.
questions.p: Everybody get right to talk for village meeting until dem reach agreement, dat na why people dey say Igbo tradition get touch of democracy.

questions.q: Which of the following was the primary reason Lord Lugard introduced the system of Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria?
o: To compensate the traditional rulers for losing their sovereign powers
To overcome the severe shortage of British administrative personnel and financial resources
To completely eradicate Islamic laws and native courts
To prepare the region immediately for democratic independence
questions.e: Indirect rule was adopted chiefly because the British colonial office lacked sufficient British staff and money to run the vast territories directly. Using existing traditional systems solved this major logistical problem.
questions.p: Na because Oyinbo government no get enough money and people to manage everywhere direct, make dem use the traditional rulers work for dem.

questions.q: The French colonial policy of Assimilation aimed primarily to achieve which of the following?
o: Transform African subjects into French citizens by instilling French culture and values
Grant absolute political independence to all French West African colonies
Establish a separate currency and army for each individual African colony
Preserve indigenous African cultures and traditional political structures unchanged
questions.e: Assimilation was built on the belief that French culture was superior and that Africans could be culturally transformed into Frenchmen if they adopted French language, laws, and lifestyle.
questions.p: Assimilation policy mean say make African people turn to French person by force, by learning their language, law and culture.

questions.q: Why did Indirect Rule encounter stiff resistance and eventual failure in the Eastern provinces of Nigeria?
o: The people in the East refused to engage in any form of Western education or commerce
The French government actively sabotaged British administration in Eastern Nigeria
The Eastern societies were strictly feudal and monarchical under powerful emirs
The British appointed Warrant Chiefs who had no traditional legitimacy or roots among the people
questions.e: Unlike the North where centralized emirates existed, the East was largely acephalous. The British imposed Warrant Chiefs, which caused deep resentment and led to events like the Aba Women's Riot of 1929.
questions.p: Wahala happen for East because British put Warrant Chiefs wey people no know before, and this one spark up anger like the Aba Women Riot.

questions.q: Which major factor forced the French to gradually abandon Assimilation in favor of Association?
o: An order from the United Nations to grant immediate independence to African colonies
The overwhelming success and complete cultural conversion of all West Africans
The heavy financial burden and fierce resistance from educated Africans who demanded equal rights
The complete absence of any traditional rulers in French West Africa
questions.e: Assimilation proved too expensive to maintain and created a group of educated Africans who demanded full French political rights, forcing France to shift to Association which respected cultural differences.
questions.p: Assimilation come too expensive, plus educated Africans con dey ask for equal right like real French people, na im make dem change am to Association.

questions.q: How did the Indirect Rule system differ structurally between Northern and Southern Nigeria?
o: In the North, traditional political structures were preserved and utilized, while in the South, new administrative chiefs had to be invented
In the North, Emirs ruled directly under British supervision, whereas in the South, traditional rulers had no advisory roles
In the South, the Emirs held supreme military power, while in the North, British Governors held total authority
