questions.q: A group of students in Kaduna State is asked to list factors that usually shape public opinion in a democratic society. Which of the following items does NOT belong to that list?
o: Religious beliefs
Personal height of citizens
Level of education
Mass media reportage
questions.e: Public opinion is shaped by things like education, religion, and the media because these affect how people think about issues. A person's physical height has nothing to do with how they form opinions on public matters.
questions.p: Public opinion dey shape by education, religion and media because dis ones dey affect how people dey think about matter. But person height no get anything to do with how dem dey form opinion on public issue.

questions.q: In two neighbouring villages, Umuahia A and Umuahia B, the children grow up with different political attitudes because one village has mission schools that stress civic duty while the other relies mainly on traditional elders' teachings. This difference in political attitudes between the two villages is best explained by the concept of:
o: Electoral behaviour
Public opinion
Political socialisation
Citizenship education
questions.e: Political socialisation is the lifelong process by which people learn political values and attitudes from agents like schools, family, and elders. The different agents (mission schools versus elders) in the two villages explain why the children develop different political orientations.
questions.p: Political socialisation na di process wey person dey learn political values from agents like school, family and elders. Because di two villages get different agents (mission school versus elders), na why di pikin dem get different political attitude.

questions.q: A Lagos-based magazine claims that 80% of Nigerians support a new tax policy, but the survey was conducted only among wealthy businesspeople in Victoria Island. A trained analyst would say this result is unreliable mainly because of:
o: Political apathy
Censorship
Propaganda
Sampling bias
questions.e: Sampling bias happens when a survey only questions a narrow, unrepresentative group instead of a cross-section of the whole population, making the result inaccurate. Here, wealthy Victoria Island businesspeople cannot represent the views of all Nigerians, so the 80% figure is misleading.
questions.p: Sampling bias na when survey only ask small group wey no represent everybody, so di result no go correct. Since na only rich Victoria Island business people dem ask, di 80% figure no fit show wetin all Nigerians think.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the civil service in Nigeria?
o: The body of permanent, paid officials who implement government policies in ministries and departments
The elected members of the National Assembly who make laws for the federation
The group of political appointees who determine government policies
The judicial officers who interpret laws in the law courts
questions.e: The civil service consists of permanent, salaried officials who carry out government policies but do not make them. Legislators, political appointees and judges belong to other arms or categories of government, not the civil service.
questions.p: Civil service na di permanent workers wey dey collect salary and dey carry out government policies, dem no dey make di policies. Legislators, political appointees and judges na different category entirely, no be civil service.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the civil service from the wider public service in Nigeria?
o: Civil service workers earn higher salaries than all other public service workers
The civil service is elected while the public service is appointed
The civil service covers only workers in core government ministries and departments, while the public service also includes employees of public corporations, the judiciary and the armed forces
The civil service exists only at state level while the public service exists only at federal level
questions.e: The civil service is a narrower term referring to officials in ministries, departments and agencies that carry out routine administration. The public service is broader, covering these plus workers in public corporations, courts, the military and police.
questions.p: Civil service na di small part wey be ministries and departments workers wey dey do normal admin work. Public service na di big umbrella wey cover civil service plus public corporations, courts, military and police workers.

questions.q: A government ministry depends almost entirely on yearly budget allocation from the Ministry of Finance to run its activities. A public corporation that supplies water to a city, however, gets part of its money from selling water to customers in addition to government subvention, and it has its own legal identity separate from the ministry. Based on this situation, which statement best explains why public corporations enjoy greater operational autonomy than ordinary ministries?
o: Public corporations can generate part of their revenue internally and, having separate legal personality, can enter contracts and manage funds with less day-to-day ministerial control
Public corporations are not required to render account to any government body since they generate their own funds
Public corporations receive no funding at all from government and operate exactly like private companies
Public corporations are exempted from all government policies because they are privately owned
questions.e: Because a corporation has its own legal personality and can earn internal revenue, it can sign contracts and manage its budget with less direct ministerial interference than a ministry that relies solely on treasury funds. It still remains accountable to government through its supervising ministry and audits.
questions.p: Since corporation get im own legal personality and dey make money from wetin e dey sell, e fit sign contract and manage im money without too much ministry control. E still dey answerable to government through im supervising ministry and audit, no be say e free complete.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system, which title was held by the chief military commander who led the emir's army into battle?
o: Waziri
Madawaki
Galadima
Sarkin Fada
questions.e: The Madawaki was the title of the chief military commander in the Hausa-Fulani system, responsible for leading the emir's army in war. The Waziri was the chief adviser, the Galadima often administered the capital, and the Sarkin Fada supervised the palace.
questions.p: Madawaki na the title wey dem give the army commander wey dey lead the emir soja go war. Waziri na the main adviser, Galadima dey manage capital, Sarkin Fada dey oversee palace matters.

questions.q: In the old Oyo Empire, the Oyo Mesi was a council of principal chiefs, headed by the Bashorun, that could check the Alaafin's power. How many principal chiefs made up this council?
o: Five
Twelve
Nine
Seven
questions.e: The Oyo Mesi was made up of seven principal chiefs, led by the Bashorun, who advised the Alaafin and could also check his excesses. This number is a well-established fact about Oyo Empire administration.
questions.p: Oyo Mesi na council of seven big chiefs, Bashorun dey lead dem, and dem get power to advise and even check Alaafin if e dey misbehave. Na seven chiefs dem dey use for dis council.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Igbo society, which institution allowed a wealthy and respected man to gain political and social influence by paying for an expensive, prestigious title?
o: Ozo title society
Age-grade system
Osu caste practice
Umuada association
questions.e: The Ozo title society was an institution in Igbo land where a man of means could pay to take a prestigious title, which raised his social status and gave him political influence in the community. Age-grades organised people by age for communal duties, Umuada was for married daughters of the lineage, and Osu referred to an outcast class, not a title system.
questions.p: Ozo title society na where rich and respected man go pay money take important title, wey go give am status and political power for im community. Age-grade na people wey dem group by age for work, Umuada na married daughters group, Osu na outcast class, no be title society.

questions.q: Under British colonial policy in Africa, which statement best defines the system known as Indirect Rule?
o: Direct administration of colonies by European officials without any local involvement
Governing the people through existing traditional rulers who worked under the supervision of colonial officials
Complete military occupation with no form of local administration at all
Granting full citizenship and voting rights of the colonial power to all Africans
questions.e: Indirect Rule meant the British ruled through traditional chiefs and emirs, who took orders from colonial Residents. This saved money and manpower while still keeping real control in British hands.
questions.p: Indirect Rule na where British dey rule through native chiefs and emirs, but dem dey report to British Residents. E dey save British money and workers, but British still dey hold the real power.

questions.q: Lord Lugard chose to model Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria on an existing political structure because it already had organised chiefs, courts and tax systems. Which structure was this?
o: The Igbo village council system
The Benin palace guild system
The Sokoto Caliphate emirate system
The Yoruba obaship confederacy
questions.e: The Sokoto Caliphate already had emirs, Islamic courts and an organised tax (zakat/jangali) system before the British arrived. Lugard simply placed British Residents above the emirs instead of creating a new system from scratch.
questions.p: Sokoto Caliphate already get emirs, courts and tax system before British come. Lugard just put British Resident on top of the emirs instead of starting new system.

questions.q: Unlike the British, the French ran their West African colonies as a highly centralised and direct system of administration. This means that:
o: African traditional kingdoms kept full independent authority over their territories
Local rulers in French colonies could make laws without approval from Paris
French colonies used the same House of Chiefs arrangement as the British colonies
All real administrative power flowed from Paris through appointed French officials, with African chiefs acting only as agents carrying out orders
questions.e: French policy treated colonies as extensions of France itself, so power was centralised in Paris and passed down through Governors-General to French-appointed chiefs. These chiefs had no independent authority like emirs under British Indirect Rule; they simply executed French orders.
questions.p: French dey see their colonies as part of France, so power dey come from Paris through French Governor to the chiefs wey dem appoint. Dis chiefs no get independent power like emirs for British system; dem just dey carry out French orders.

questions.q: Because Eastern Nigeria lacked large centralised kingdoms like those in the North, the British created a new class of local government agents to help collect tax and keep order. These agents were called:
o: Warrant Chiefs
District Officers
Residents
Emirs
questions.e: Since many Eastern communities were organised in small, independent village groups rather than centralised kingdoms, the British appointed local men and gave them a 'warrant' of authority to act as chiefs, even where such a position never existed before. These became known as Warrant Chiefs.
questions.p: For Eastern Nigeria, plenty communities no get big central kingdom like North. So British go appoint some men, give dem 'warrant' make dem act as chief, even though such position no dey before. Na dem be Warrant Chiefs.

questions.q: Which newspaper, founded by Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe in 1937, became one of the most powerful tools for spreading nationalist ideas and criticising colonial rule across Nigeria?
o: Daily Times
Nigerian Tribune
The Comet
West African Pilot
questions.e: The West African Pilot, established by Azikiwe in 1937, used bold articles to awaken political awareness and attack colonial policies. It became a major voice for nationalist agitation before independence.
questions.p: Na West African Pilot, wey Azikiwe start am for 1937, dem dey use spread nationalist ideas and dey talk against colonial rule. E be like strong mouthpiece wey many Nigerians dey read.

questions.q: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), formed in 1944, was set up mainly to
o: serve purely as a trade union for railway workers
unite Nigerians and Cameroonians in a broad-based nationalist movement against colonial policies
promote exclusively cultural festivals among the Igbo people
create a single political party meant only for Northern Nigeria
questions.e: The NCNC brought together various Nigerian and Cameroonian groups to form a strong, nationwide movement demanding greater political participation and an end to colonial domination. It was not limited to one region or ethnic group.
questions.p: Dem form NCNC for 1944 to bring Nigerians and Cameroonians togeda so dem fit fight colonial rule as one big group. E no be only for one region or one tribe.

questions.q: A major reason Nigerian nationalists strongly criticised the Richards Constitution of 1946 was that it
o: abolished all native courts across the country
removed British officials completely from the Legislative Council
introduced regionalism and major constitutional changes without adequate consultation with Nigerian leaders
granted Nigeria full self-government ahead of schedule
questions.e: Nigerian leaders were angry that Governor Richards introduced far-reaching changes, including dividing Nigeria into three regions, without proper consultation with them. This lack of consultation fuelled nationalist protests and demands for more Nigerian involvement in governance.
questions.p: Richards Constitution bring regionalism and big changes but e no first ask Nigerian leaders well well. Na dis kind one-sided decision make nationalists vex and dey agitate for better involvement.

questions.q: After the Second World War, many Nigerian ex-servicemen who had fought for Britain returned home to face unemployment and racial discrimination despite their wartime sacrifices. How did this situation mainly affect Nigerian nationalism?
o: It pushed many ex-servicemen to join and strengthen the agitation for self-rule and fair treatment
It caused the ex-servicemen to form a new colonial police force loyal to Britain
It made the ex-servicemen migrate permanently to Britain to seek better treatment
It made the colonial government immediately grant independence to avoid unrest
questions.e: Having fought and suffered for Britain, the ex-servicemen expected fair treatment and reward at home. Instead they faced neglect, so they joined nationalist movements, bringing discipline, organisation and urgency to the independence struggle.
questions.p: Dem soldiers wey fight for Britain come back meet no job and bad treatment for dia own country. Dat kain disappointment push many of dem to join nationalist struggle well well, add strong organisation give am.

questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1945 is chiefly remembered in Nigeria's constitutional history for introducing which feature?
o: Internal self-government for all three regions at the same time
A full federal system with regional premiers and cabinets
The principle of regionalism by grouping Nigeria into three regions for legislative discussion
Direct election of members into the Legislative Council by the people
questions.e: Richards' main contribution was dividing Nigeria into Northern, Western and Eastern regions, each with its own House for discussing bills before they went to the central Legislative Council. Direct elections, premiers and self-government came much later under other constitutions.
questions.p: Richards Constitution main work na to divide Nigeria into three regions wey go dey discuss bills before dem reach central council. Election by all people, premiers and self-government come later under other constitutions.

questions.q: By the end of the 1957 Constitutional Conference, which two regions of Nigeria had been granted internal self-government ahead of the North?
o: Eastern and Northern regions
Western region alone, with no other region granted self-government
Northern and Western regions
Western and Eastern regions
questions.e: The Western and Eastern Regions achieved internal self-government in 1957 because their leaders pushed strongly for early self-rule. The Northern Region, due to concerns about readiness in education and administration, delayed and only got internal self-government in 1959.
questions.p: Western and Eastern Region get internal self-government for 1957 because dia leaders push hard for am. Northern Region fear say dem no ready well-well for education and administration, so dem get their own self-government for 1959.

questions.q: During the constitutional talks leading to Nigeria's independence, Northern Region leaders were initially reluctant to accept an early self-government date (such as 1956) proposed by some Southern politicians. What was the main reason for this reluctance?
o: They preferred that the British continue to rule Nigeria indefinitely without any change
They feared the North lagged behind in Western education and trained manpower needed to run a modern government
They wanted the North to break away completely and form a separate country
They insisted that the federal capital be relocated from Lagos to the North before any self-government talks
questions.e: Northern leaders, aware that Western education and the civil service had developed more in the South, worried that early self-government would let Southern-trained Nigerians dominate a united Nigeria. This made them push for a slower, phased approach rather than outright secession or permanent colonial rule.
questions.p: Northern leaders sabi say Western education and civil service dey more for South, so dem fear say South go dominate if self-government come too fast. Na why dem want slow slow process, no be say dem wan break away or make British stay forever.

questions.q: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, who became Nigeria's Head of State, replacing the British monarch who had been represented by a Governor-General?
o: President
Premier
Prime Minister
Governor
questions.e: The 1963 Constitution made Nigeria a republic, so the Queen was replaced by a Nigerian President as Head of State. The Prime Minister remained Head of Government, while Premiers headed the regions.
questions.p: 1963 Constitution turn Nigeria to republic, so Nigerian President take over as Head of State instead of di Queen. Prime Minister still dey as Head of Government, Premiers dey lead di regions.

questions.q: Which of the following matters falls under the Concurrent Legislative List in the 1999 Constitution, meaning both the National Assembly and a State House of Assembly can validly make laws on it?
o: External affairs
Electricity generation and distribution
Currency and coinage
Immigration
questions.e: Electricity generation and distribution is on the Concurrent List, so both federal and state legislatures can make laws on it, though federal law prevails if there is a conflict. Currency, external affairs and immigration are strictly on the Exclusive List for the federal government alone.
questions.p: Electricity generation and distribution dey for Concurrent List, so both National Assembly and State Assembly fit make law on top am, but federal law go win if clash happen. Currency, external affairs and immigration na only federal government fit touch dem, dem dey Exclusive List.

questions.q: The federal character principle, first entrenched in the 1979 Constitution and retained in the 1999 Constitution, was mainly introduced to achieve which of the following?
o: Direct election of traditional rulers into the Senate
Automatic creation of more states to balance population figures
Fair representation of Nigeria's various ethnic and state groups in government appointments
Equal distribution of mineral resources among the states
questions.e: The federal character principle requires that appointments to federal institutions reflect the diversity of Nigeria's states and ethnic groups, preventing domination by any single group. It is about representation in government, not resource sharing, state creation, or electing traditional rulers.
questions.p: Federal character principle mean say wen dem dey appoint people for federal jobs, dem must carry all states and ethnic groups follow, so one group no go dominate. E no concern resource sharing, state creation, or election of traditional rulers.

questions.q: At independence in 1960, Nigeria was a federation of three regions - Northern, Eastern and Western. Which additional region was created shortly before the 1963 Republican Constitution took effect, bringing the total number of regions to four?
o: Niger Delta Region
Benue Region
North-Central Region
Mid-Western Region
questions.e: The Mid-Western Region was carved out of the former Western Region in 1963, making Nigeria a four-region federation just before the Republican Constitution came into force. The other options are not regions that existed at that time.
questions.p: Dem carve Mid-Western Region comot from di old Western Region for 1963, so Nigeria become four-region federation before di Republican Constitution start. Di oda options no be regions wey dey exist dat time.

questions.q: Who became Nigeria's first military Head of State, following the coup d'etat of January 1966?
o: Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi
Sani Abacha
Yakubu Gowon
Murtala Mohammed
questions.e: After the January 1966 coup, Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi took over as Head of State, making him Nigeria's first military ruler. Gowon took over later that same year after a counter-coup.
questions.p: After di January 1966 coup, Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi take over as Head of State, so na him be di first military ruler for Nigeria. Gowon come take over later dat same year afta counter-coup.

questions.q: Under military administrations in Nigeria, the body that served as the highest policy-making organ, usually made up of the Head of State and senior military officers, was called the:
o: National Council of Ministers
Council of State
Supreme Military Council
Federal Executive Council
questions.e: The Supreme Military Council (sometimes renamed Armed Forces Ruling Council) was the apex body under military rule, where major policies and decrees were decided. The Federal Executive Council handled day-to-day administration but was subordinate to it.
questions.p: Di Supreme Military Council (later dem call am Armed Forces Ruling Council) na di highest body under military rule, na dem dey decide big policies and decrees. Federal Executive Council dey handle normal wahala but dem dey under di Supreme Military Council.

questions.q: A major criticism of military rule in Nigeria, from the perspective of federalism, is that it tended to:
o: grant more legislative powers to state houses of assembly
concentrate power at the centre because of the military's hierarchical command structure
increase the number of political parties operating in the states
restore full legislative autonomy to traditional rulers
questions.e: The military operates on a chain of command from the Head of State downward, so this same style was carried into governance, pulling power away from the states to the centre. This weakened true federalism, which requires shared and balanced powers between federal and state levels.
questions.p: Military dey work like chain of command, from Head of State to everybody under am, so dem bring dis same style enter governance, and e pull power comot from states go centre. Dis one weak true federalism wey suppose share power well-well between federal and state.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, decrees issued by the Head of State typically had which of the following effects on existing laws?
o: They required approval by the Senate before they could take effect
They could only amend state laws but never federal laws
They had no binding legal effect until confirmed by the Supreme Court
They could override the constitution and any existing law that was inconsistent with them
questions.e: Military decrees were given supremacy over the constitution and ordinary laws, often including clauses that barred the courts (ouster clauses) from questioning them. This made decrees the main legal tool of military rule.
questions.p: Military decrees dey pass constitution and normal laws, and many times dem dey put clause wey block court from questioning dem (ouster clause). Na so decree come be di main legal tool wey military government dey use rule.

questions.q: According to the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended), how many local government areas are officially recognised in the country?
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution lists exactly 774 local government areas in Nigeria. This number is fixed in the constitution and is a basic fact every candidate should know.
questions.p: Di 1999 Constitution show say Nigeria get 774 local government areas. Dis number dey fixed inside di constitution, na basic fact wey every candidate suppose sabi.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of the local government system of administration in Nigeria?
o: It brings government and its services closer to the people at the grassroots
It removes the need for state governments to exist
It concentrates all legislative powers in the hands of the federal government
It eliminates the role of traditional rulers in community affairs
questions.e: Local government is the tier of government closest to the people in villages and towns, so it helps deliver services like primary healthcare, markets and sanitation directly to them. The other options describe things local government does not do.
questions.p: Local government na di tier of government wey close pass to di people for village and town, so e dey bring services like health post, market and clean environment reach dem direct. Di other options no be wetin local government dey do.

questions.q: In the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the specific functions assigned to local government councils are contained in which schedule?
o: Fifth Schedule
Second Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Third Schedule
questions.e: The Fourth Schedule of the 1999 Constitution spells out the functions of local government councils, such as construction of roads, markets and primary education. Candidates must know this because it is often tested directly.
questions.p: Di Fourth Schedule of di 1999 Constitution na im dey list di work wey local government councils suppose do, like road, market and primary school. Dis one dey common for exam so candidates need sabi am well.

questions.q: Local government in Nigeria is commonly described as the 'third tier' of government. This description is based mainly on the fact that it:
o: was the third tier of government to be created historically in Nigeria
has the smallest population compared to the federal and state governments
generates the third largest share of government revenue in the country
occupies the third level in the hierarchical structure of government, below the federal and state governments
questions.e: The term 'third tier' refers to local government's position in the structure of governance, coming after the federal government (first tier) and the state government (second tier). It is about rank in the governmental hierarchy, not about population, history of creation, or revenue size.
questions.p: Dem dey call local government 'third tier' because of how e dey sit for di government structure, after federal (first tier) and state (second tier). E no concern population, history of how dem create am, or how much money e dey generate.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended), the primary responsibility for formulating Nigeria's foreign policy rests with which arm or officer of government?
o: The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs
The Judiciary, through the Supreme Court
The National Assembly, through its Senate Committee on Foreign Affairs
The President, acting through the executive arm of government
questions.e: The Constitution vests executive power, including the conduct of external relations, in the President. The President, assisted by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, formulates and directs Nigeria's foreign policy. The National Assembly only ratifies treaties; it does not formulate policy.
questions.p: Di Constitution give executive power to President, dat one include how Nigeria dey relate wit oda kontri. President, wit di help of Minister of Foreign Affairs, na im dey make di foreign policy. National Assembly na only to confam treaty, dem no dey make di policy.

questions.q: Nigeria's active role in founding the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) in 1963 was mainly an expression of which foreign policy objective?
o: Securing permanent membership of the UN Security Council
Promotion of economic diplomacy with Western powers
Promotion of African unity, solidarity and decolonisation
Protection of Nigerian citizens living abroad
questions.e: The OAU was formed to unite African states, support the liberation of colonies still under foreign rule, and encourage cooperation among African nations. Nigeria, as a leading African power, championed this objective as central to its Afrocentric foreign policy. It was not primarily about trade deals or UN seats.
questions.p: Dem form OAU make African kontris unite, support countries wey still dey under colonial rule, and work together as one. Nigeria, as big African kontri, support dis objective well because im foreign policy dey focus on Africa. E no be about trade deal or UN Security Council seat.

questions.q: During the Cold War era, Nigeria officially pursued a policy of non-alignment. Based on this principle, which of the following actions would have been MOST inconsistent with Nigeria's stated foreign policy?
o: Accepting technical assistance from both the United States and the Soviet Union
Signing a defence pact that ties Nigeria's armed forces exclusively to one superpower bloc
Trading with countries from both the Western and Eastern blocs
Sending delegates to Non-Aligned Movement conferences
questions.e: Non-alignment meant Nigeria refused to be permanently tied to either the Western (capitalist) or Eastern (communist) bloc during the Cold War, so as to relate freely with all nations. Signing an exclusive military pact with one bloc would contradict this neutrality by committing Nigeria firmly to one side. The other options (receiving aid from both sides, trading with both, joining NAM) all fit non-alignment.
questions.p: Non-alignment mean Nigeria no wan tie imsef strong strong to eida di Western (capitalist) or Eastern (communist) side during Cold War, so dat e fit relate well wit everybody. If Nigeria sign military agreement wey go make im army dey only follow one side, dat one go spoil di neutral stand. Di oda options dey match wit non-alignment well well.

questions.q: Which of the following international organisations has its membership restricted only to countries located on the African continent?
o: African Union (AU)
United Nations (UN)
Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
Commonwealth of Nations
questions.e: The African Union is made up only of African states, unlike the UN, Commonwealth, and OPEC, which have members from different continents. This makes it a purely continental organisation.
questions.p: African Union na only African kontries dey inside am. UN, Commonwealth, and OPEC get members from different continents, but AU na only Africa.

questions.q: Under the ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, what right is granted to citizens of member states travelling within the sub-region?
o: The right to hold a government ministerial post in another member state
The right to enter and stay in another member state for up to 90 days without a visa
Automatic citizenship of any member state after six months
The right to vote in the national elections of any member state
questions.e: The ECOWAS Protocol allows citizens of member states to enter another member country visa-free and stay for up to 90 days, promoting regional integration. It does not grant automatic citizenship, voting rights, or government positions.
questions.p: ECOWAS Protocol give citizens power to waka enter another member kontri witout visa and stay for 90 days. E no mean say dem go automatically become citizen, vote, or hold government post.

questions.q: A member country of OPEC wants to help raise the global price of crude oil. Based on OPEC's usual method of controlling oil prices, what should this country do?
o: Increase its production above its agreed quota
Withdraw from OPEC and sell oil at any price it wants
Fix oil prices directly with each buyer nation
Comply with an OPEC-agreed cut in its production quota
questions.e: OPEC controls global oil prices mainly by agreeing on production quotas among members; cutting output reduces supply and pushes prices up. Increasing production or acting independently would work against this goal.
questions.p: OPEC dey control oil price by make members agree to cut how much oil dem go produce; if supply reduce, price go rise. If kontri increase production or waka comot to sell anyhow, e no go help raise price.

questions.q: The Commonwealth of Nations mainly promotes cooperation among its member countries in which of these areas?
o: Adoption of a single currency and customs union
Formation of a joint military defence pact
Democracy, human rights, trade and development cooperation
Religious integration policies for all members
questions.e: The Commonwealth focuses on promoting democracy, human rights, trade, and development among its member states, which share historical ties to Britain. It is not a military alliance, a currency union, or a religious body.
questions.p: Commonwealth dey focus on promote democracy, human rights, trade, and development among im members wey get historical connection to Britain. E no be military alliance, currency union, or religious group.
